sections.h2: Decatur County tax offices in Bainbridge
sections.html:
Two offices in the Bainbridge courthouse split the work. One prepares the digest, mails the bills and takes payment. The other, the assessors, puts a value on every real and personal parcel. Both operate inside the courthouse on West Water Street.

Collection happens on the ground floor of the courthouse, 112 W. Water St., Monday to Friday between 8 and 5. Call (229) 248-3021 about property tax, (229) 248-3019 for motor vehicles or (229) 248-3009 for the tag office. Letters go to P.O. Box 246, Bainbridge, and decaturcountytax.com is the office's website. Valuation questions go to (229) 248-3008 or to P.O. Box 1106 in the same city.

Roughly 20,000 property tax bills and 3,300 mobile home bills go out each year. What comes in is sent on to the state, county, schools, library and cities every other week.

sections.h2: Decatur County housing at a glance
sections.html:
The population has been flat lately: 27,842 in 2010, 29,367 in 2020, and an estimate of 29,432 for 2025. Bainbridge holds the courthouse. Attapulgus, Bainbridge and Climax are cities, and Brinson is a town, so check whether your parcel also owes a city bill.

  • Housing units: 13,601, with 10,621 households.
  • Owner-occupied share: 62.1 percent.
  • Typical value of an owned home, 2020 to 2024: $158,800.
  • Typical rent: $838 monthly.
  • Housing permits in 2025: 135.

With a slow-moving market and modest values, a back-tax balance or an out-of-date record can weigh more on a sale here than it would at a higher price point.

Decatur County sets December 20 as the yearly deadline for property tax and April 1 for mobile homes.

Decatur County tax dates
TaskDate or deadline
Real and personal property billsDue December 20
Mobile home billsDue April 1
Returns, conservation and agricultural applicationsJanuary 1 through April 1
Homestead applicationDuring the year, up to April 1 of the following year
Appeal of an assessment45 days from the mailing date printed on the notice
Board of Assessors meetingSecond Tuesday of each month, 8:30 a.m., Grand Jury Room

Georgia lets a county choose December 1 or November 15 instead, or bill in installments, and interest holds off for 60 days after the bill is postmarked. Ask the commissioner what interest and penalties apply to a late bill, and go by the date printed on your own bill.

sections.h2: How to appeal and file forms
sections.html:
Look at the top right corner of the assessment notice. The final appeal day is printed there, 45 days after mailing, and it moves from year to year, so rely on your own paper.

The assessors' office also receives returns for real and personal property and applications for homestead, conservation use, preferential agricultural assessment, forest land conservation use assessment and Freeport. Blank forms are on the Department of Revenue's forms page, and completed ones can go in by email, ordinary mail or the drop box outside the courthouse.

  • Returns and special-use applications: January 1 through April 1.
  • Homestead under Code Section 48-5-44: file once the house is your primary residence, through April 1 of the next year.
  • Property records and parcel data: the county's qPublic site at qpublic.net/ga/decatur.
  • Board sessions: second Tuesday monthly, 8:30 in the morning, Grand Jury Room.

sections.h2: Will an appraiser visit my Decatur County property?
sections.html:
Possibly. State law, O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1, lets assessor representatives with proper identification enter property during normal business hours. Reasons include permits that were issued, a return of value, a revaluation of part or all of the county, parcel sales and appeal reviews.

The office uses building permits and other sources to update its records, and appraisers visit where improvements were made or information looks wrong. If you added a room, finished a garage or tore something down, the permit trail may already have reached the assessors. Check what the record shows before a buyer's agent does.

The assessors also assemble the tax digest, the compilation of property values, motor vehicle values, timber values and exemption amounts that goes to the State Revenue Commissioner. A change in your parcel's record flows into that report.

sections.h2: Selling with back tax or a mobile home bill
sections.html:
Only the commissioner can quote a payoff. Phone (229) 248-3021, give the parcel number and your expected closing date, and ask for the number in writing.

  • A mobile home has its own April 1 bill, so check that account separately from any land.
  • Cities in the county levy their own tax, and the city clerk bills it unless the city and county agreed to a single bill. Ask the commissioner whether yours is combined.
  • Refunds for tax wrongly collected must be requested within three years of the payment.
  • If the house passed through an estate, ask the assessors which documents they need to update the owner before the bill goes out.

Bills are charged to the owner on January 1 under Georgia's rules, so the sale contract should state who covers the part of the year after closing. Have the settlement agent send the payoff directly to the commissioner and keep the receipt.

A little groundwork keeps a closing on schedule. First, pull your parcel on the qPublic site and compare the record to the house as it stands today. Second, call the commissioner for a written balance. Third, ask the assessors whether a homestead, conservation or agricultural application is on file and whether it will carry over to the buyer.

If the bill is unpaid when the contract is signed, the title company will want it cleared at closing. A buyer paying cash usually still asks for the same paperwork, though the closing can be quicker because no lender is waiting on a tax certification.

On closing day, the settlement agent should hold the payoff figure and send it straight to the commissioner's office at 112 W. Water St. or by mail to P.O. Box 246. Ask for a receipt that shows the parcel number, and keep it with your closing papers. If the sale happens after the December 20 deadline and the bill is still open, interest and penalties may already be running, so get the current number rather than relying on the amount printed on last month's bill.

If you own a mobile home on the lot, remember it has its own account and its own April 1 date. A buyer's title agent will look for both accounts, so settle them together.

Questions about the value on a parcel or a missing form go to the assessors at (229) 248-3008. Questions about what you owe go to the commissioner. Keeping the two straight avoids being passed back and forth between desks while a buyer waits.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Decatur County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the courthouse, 112 W. Water St., Bainbridge, GA 39817, first floor. The counter runs weekdays 8 to 5, and the property tax number is (229) 248-3021.

faqs.q: What is the Decatur County payment deadline?
faqs.a: December 20, with mobile homes due April 1. Confirm against your own bill, since a county may adopt another date.

faqs.q: How many days does a Decatur County owner have to appeal?
faqs.a: Forty-five days counted from the mailing date of the notice. The last filing day is printed in the notice's top right corner.

faqs.q: Does Decatur County have a drop box for tax forms?
faqs.a: Yes. The assessors list a drop box outside the courthouse, along with email and regular mail, as ways to submit forms and applications.

faqs.q: When does the Board of Assessors meet?
faqs.a: On the second Tuesday of each month at 8:30 a.m. in the Grand Jury Room.
